newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: South American port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: South American port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ARGENTINA, June 3 - Santa Fe - No vessels berthed, no vessels in roads, no vessels due. Max. draft 25 ft. 00 in. at access channel. Diamante - one vessel berthed loading rice, no vessels in roads, no vessels due. Max. draft 25 ft. 0 in. at passage km 520. San Lorenzo - six vessels berthed of which 1 loading SBMP, 1 loading soya, 1 discharging chemical products, 1 loading by-products, 1 loading linoil, 1 loading maize, 4 vessels in roads, 29 vessels due at 6 terminals during the coming week. Pasa berth draft, 19 ft. 01 in. fw. Max. recommended draft 32 ft. 09 in. fw high tide.

Rosario - eight vessels berthed of which 2 loading maize, 1 repairs, 1 discharging fertiliser, 1 loading fruit, 1 loading SBO, 1 loading SBM, 1 loading sorghum, 5 vessels in roads, 15 vessels due during the coming week. Max. recommended draft 32 ft. 09 in. fw high tide. Villa Constitucion - no vessels berthed, no vessels in roads, 3 vessels due. Elevator berths max. draft 22 ft. 0 in. fw. San Nicolas - four vessels berthed of which 1 loading maize, 1 loading steel products, 1 discharging general cargo, 1 discharging iron ore, 1 vessel in roads, 2 vessels due during next week. Max. recommended draft 33 ft. 03 in. fw high tide.

San Pedro - no vessels berthed, no vessels in roads, 2 vessels due. Max. recommended draft 33 ft. 03 in. fw high tide. Buenos Aires - eighteen vessels in port, 22 vessels due during the week. Max. draft 31 ft. 06 in. fw high tide NAABSA (guided by entrance channel). Dock Sud - max. recommended draft 28/29 ft. fw high tide NAABSA (guided by entrance channel). Necochea - five vessels berthed of which 2 loading wheat, 1 loading maize, 1 loading SFMP, 12 vessels in roads, 16 vessels due during the week, max. draft at entrance channel is 40 ft. 0 in. bw. Bahia Blanca - five vessels berthed of which 2 loading maize, 1 loading sorghum, 1 loading fuel oil, 1 discharging Dap, 3 vessels in roads, 10 vessels due during the week. draft depends on each berth.

BRAZIL, June 3 - Salvador - The dispute between the stevedores and the port operators in Salvador continues. The stevedores interrupted their work-to-rule action over the last weekend, but resume their action again on 2 June.

Vitoria - vessels berthed, 1 bulk wheat discharger, 1 granite loader. Tubarao, 3 iron ore loaders. Praia Mole, 3 steel products loaders, 2 coal dischargers. Ubu, 1 iron ore loader. Twenty-two vessels waiting in roads. Santos - vessels berthed, 4 full container loaders/dischargers, 1 full container loader, 1 bulk cement, 1 heavy load loader, 1 bulk chemical products discharger, 1 general cargo discharger, 1 bulk soya loader, 2 fertiliser dischargers, 1 bulk pellets loader, 4 sugar loaders, 2 juice loaders, 14 vessels waiting in roads, 78 vessels due during next 7 days.

Private terminals, Cosipa, 2 steel products loaders, 1 iron ore discharger. Ultrafertil, 1 bulk sulphur discharger. Rio Grande - vessels berthed, 1 full container loader, 1 soya loader, 1 soya oil loader, 2 wheat dischargers, 29 vessels due during next 10 days. Rio de Janeiro - vessels berthed, 1 wheat discharger, 2 general cargo/steel products dischargers, 1 container/general cargo discharger, 3 general cargo dischargers, 1 oil discharger, 1 caustic soda discharger, 2 general cargo/steel products loaders, 1 container/general cargo loader, 1 container/steel products loader, 1 sugar loader. Tecon, 2 vessels, 29 vessels due during next 7 days. Sao Sebastiao - vessels berthed. Tebar, 3 vessels. Commercial quay, 1 vessel, 4 vessels waiting in roads, 6 vessels due during next 7 days.

CHILE, June 2 - Arica - Eight vessels in port. 4 berths vacant. 7 due during week. Iquique - five vessels operating. 1 berth vacant. 7 due during week. Antofagasta - one vessel berthed. 6 berths available. 14 vessels due during week for loading and discharging concentrates, bulk copper, containers and general cargo. Valparaiso - six vessels berthed working normally. 3 berths vacant. One berth out of service due to enlargement until April 1998. 9 due during week. 1 days delay expected. San Antonio - eight vessels operating. 2 berths vacant. 15 vessels due during week. Port busy, but no waiting time.

Conception Bay ports - Talcahuano - no vessels berthed. 2 due. No vessels waiting in roads. San Vicente - three vessels berthed, operating normally. 8 due during week. Navy pier (MOLO 500) 1 vessel berthed in terminal. No vessels due. Steel pier - 2 vessels berthed in terminal. No vessels due during week. Oil Terminal - 1 vessel in terminal, no vessels due. Lirquen - five vessels berthed. 3 berths vacant. 6 vessels due during week. Penco - no vessels due. Puerto Montt - two vessels in port. 1 passenger vessel. 5 vessels due during week. Punta Arenas - four vessels berthed. 10 due during the week.

PERU, June 2 - Callao - Eight vessels in bay, 7 in pier (general cargo/containers). No berthing delays. Paita - one fishmeal vessel in pier. No berthing delays. Bayovar, Pisco - no vessels. Talara - one vessel in bay, 1 in pier (oil). No berthing delays. Chimbote - three vessels in bay, 4 in pier (fishmeal). No berthing delays. Ilo - one copper vessels in pier. No berthing delays.
VENEZUELA, June 2 - Puerto Cabello - Six vessels anchored. 12 vessels berthed of which 5 grain, 5 general cargo, 1 ro/ro. Guanta - one vessel anchored. 2 general cargo vessels berthed.
